title: hotfix: SLO enforcer backoff bug + regional failover cooldown to prevent thrashing
author: Evan Park
description:
Motivation: During the 2026-02-24 incident we observed rapid regional failover and SLO-enforcer thrashing when under upstream contention. The root cause was a bug in the SLO enforcer backoff logic: the backoff counter was reset on a downstream success path and some race conditions allowed immediate re-entry into failover for region-cold-started pools. This caused repeated failovers and amplified load on healthy regions.

This PR fixes three things: 1) Correct exponential backoff implementation with jitter and a cap to avoid immediate reset on partial success; 2) Add a per-region cooldown window (configurable) that prevents repeated failover within a short window; 3) Add defensive checks and metrics so we can detect failover thrashing early and automatically raise a page before global impact.

What changed (high level):
- Fix backoff reset race in slo/enforcer: ensure backoff only decreases after sustained success window.
- Add region_failover_cooldown to routing policy and SLO enforcer state machine.
- Emit new metrics: slo.enforcer.backoff_seconds, slo.enforcer.failover_cooldown_count, slo.enforcer.thrash_detected (bool gauge).
- Add unit + integration tests covering concurrent enforcer signals and simulated region flapping.
- Update docs: runtime/operational-playbooks.md with guidance for tuning cooldown and backoff parameters.

Checklist:
- [x] Fix bug in backoff state machine
- [x] Add cooldown guardrail to regional failover
- [x] Add metrics and dashboard panels (alert rule added)
- [x] Add tests (unit + integration)
- [x] Verified in perf-canary with 2x traffic pattern that previously triggered thrashing
- [x] Release notes drafted

Notes: This is a hotfix targeting immediate stability; thresholds are conservative. Follow-up work (ENG-8830) will expose a richer tuning surface in Console and add a canary config rollout for high-traffic customers.
